# glib 0.18.5 backport

`glib-0.18.5/` is the complete crates.io `glib` 0.18.5 archive (SHA-256 `233daaf6e83ae6a12a52055f568f9d7cf4671dabb78ff9560ab6da230ce00ee5`), with only the upstream fix for [RUSTSEC-2024-0429](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html): `VariantStrIter::impl_get` now passes a mutable out-pointer to `g_variant_get_child`. The change is the two-line backport from [gtk-rs-core PR 1343](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core/pull/1343). The crate's name, version, API, and other files are unchanged so the Linux GTK3/AppIndicator tray dependencies continue to resolve together.

The desktop CI check runs `node scripts/verify-vendored-glib.mjs`. It verifies the complete vendored tree against a fingerprint of the verified crates.io archive after reversing exactly those two changed lines. `.gitattributes` preserves the crate's bytes on Windows checkouts. To independently audit the source, download `glib-0.18.5.crate` from crates.io, verify its SHA-256 above, extract it, and compare it with this directory. Run `cargo tree --locked --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -i glib@0.18.5` to confirm the Linux dependency path resolves to this local copy. On Linux with GTK3 and AppIndicator development libraries installed, run `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked -- -D warnings`, a release build, and the installed tray smoke test. macOS tests do not exercise this Linux dependency.

The advisory still applies to the original crates.io `0.18.5` archive. Cargo audit skips local path dependencies, so its absence from audit output does not prove this backport is correct. Keep the advisory in security tracking and use the source verifier and Linux runtime checks as the mitigation evidence.
